audit.whatIsWrong: The whole plan is 'bait Soul Unbound, then commit' — repeated in spikes[1], mid, whys[2], whys[3], wants.you[0], breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and report[5] — and the cooldown is never stated once.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22/19/16/13/10. Twenty-two seconds at rank 1 is the longest window Galio gets in this lane and the number is what makes 'bait it first' actionable instead of aspirational. The rest matter too: Spirit Cleave is 14s and shrinks with his attack speed, Mortal Steel is a 4-second base, and Fate Sealed is 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound 22s at rank 1, down to 10s at rank 5 — the early window is huge and it shrinks fast. Spirit Cleave 14s and falling with attack speed; Mortal Steel 4s; Fate Sealed 120s at rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (E 22/19/16/13/10; W 14, 'cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed'; Q 4; R 120/100/80)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] calls Fate Sealed 'an all-in knockup-dash', whys[6] says it 'catches you committed', and dontsFull[0] says Soul Unbound 'catches you mid-dash'.
audit.why: Fate Sealed blinks Yone behind the LAST champion in a line and pulls everyone it hit toward him — it is a pull, not a knockup, and its danger is being dragged out of position and behind him, not being airborne. Soul Unbound has no crowd control at all; it is a spirit-form self-buff and cannot catch anything. Two of the three abilities the page tells you to fear are described as doing something they do not do.
audit.corrected: Fate Sealed pulls, it does not knock up — it lands behind the last champion in the line and drags everyone it clipped back toward him, so never stand in a line with your team. Soul Unbound has no CC.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (R Fate Sealed: 'blinks behind the last champion in a line with a slash so powerful it pulls all enemies hit towards him', flags dash; E Soul Unbound flags: none)

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[2].why says 'the dash is interruptible and root-able mid-flight'.
audit.why: Justice Punch cannot be interrupted once travelling, and Yone has no root. His only crowd control is the Mortal Steel knockup at 2 Gathering Storm stacks and the Fate Sealed pull. The knockup is the one that matters to Galio, because it cancels a charging Shield of Durand before the taunt releases.
audit.corrected: Yone has no root. What breaks your combo is his second Mortal Steel — at 2 stacks it dashes him forward with a knockup that cancels the W charge.
sources: wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio (Justice Punch cannot be interrupted mid-travel; W taunt applies on recast)
champ-data/_kits/yone.json (Q: 'At 2 stacks, Mortal Steel dashes Yone forward with a gust of wind knocking enemies Airborne')

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Cleave is mentioned three times purely as damage. Its shield is never mentioned, and neither is the fact that its cooldown shrinks with his attack speed.
audit.why: Spirit Cleave shields Yone, scaling with the number of champions hit, and both its cooldown and its cast time scale with attack speed — so the longer the game runs and the more attack speed he buys, the more often that shield is up. Against a Galio whose damage arrives in one taunt-window burst, an on-demand shield is a bigger problem than the DPS the page focuses on.
audit.corrected: Spirit Cleave shields him on every cast, and its 14-second cooldown shrinks as he buys attack speed — so your burst lands into a shield more and more often as the game goes.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (W Spirit Cleave: 'Grants a shield to Yone... Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed', cooldown 14, flags shield)

audit.why: The entry's best call is already right: Way of the Hunter makes every second attack magic damage, so Shield of Durand's magic-weighted reduction only covers part of his output. spikes[0], early and wants.you[1] all state this correctly and I left the argument alone; the reduction split is 25/30/35/40/45% versus magic against 12.5/15/17.5/20/22.5% versus physical, which is exactly why 'only soaks half' is the right read.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (P Way of the Hunter: 'deals magic damage with every second Attack')

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Skill, Yone, Yone, Skill, Skill, Yone, Yone while the prose gives Level 1 to Yone outright ('Yone owns the opening'), calls Level 3 and Levels 4-5 coin flips, and calls Level 6 'the one stage that is clearly yours'.
audit.why: Level 1 and Level 6 are the two rows the chart gets exactly backwards, and those are the rows that decide whether a player contests the first wave and whether he holds his ultimate for lane.
audit.corrected: Yone, Yone, Skill, Skill, Galio, Yone, Yone — which also fits 45.31%.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer gives the range Galio pokes from.
audit.why: Winds of War is 825 against Mortal Steel's 450 and Spirit Cleave's 700. early says 'farm with Winds of War from range' with no number, so a player has no idea he owns 125 units of safety even against the longest thing Yone has.
audit.corrected: Winds of War is 825; Mortal Steel is 450 and Spirit Cleave 700. You out-range everything he owns, so farm from there and make him spend the Q dash to close.

audit.why: The packet flags "Use Hero's Entrance" as a probable wrong ability name. It is a false positive from the near-miss matcher — Hero's Entrance is correct.

edits.before: Yone owns the start: at Level 1 you have a single ability and no engage, so his Mortal Steel Q-strikes chip you while you can only farm with Winds of War from range. Don't channel Shield of Durand to block his poke — his passive splits his damage half-physical, half-magic, so the magic-amplified reduction only soaks about half of what he does. Once you hit 3 with Q-W-E, your only real punish is the Shield of Durand release-taunt into a Justice Punch knockup, but he holds Soul Unbound specifically to snap back to his body and undo it — bait that E out before you commit or your taunt catches a husk.
edits.after: Yone owns the start: at Level 1 you have a single ability and no engage, so his Mortal Steel strikes chip you while you farm with Winds of War at 825 — comfortably outside his 450 and his 700-range Spirit Cleave. Don't channel Shield of Durand to block his poke: Way of the Hunter makes every second attack magic damage, so the magic-weighted reduction only soaks about half of what he does. Once you hit 3, your one real punish is the release-taunt into a Justice Punch knockup, but he holds Soul Unbound — 22 seconds at rank 1 — specifically to snap back to his body and undo it. Bait that E out before you commit.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a coin-flip skirmish — you can land Justice Punch into a released Shield of Durand taunt if he burns Soul Unbound first, but he resets the trade for free if he holds it. Level 6 is your one clear stage: Hero's Entrance means a losing duel doesn't matter, because you can R to a sidelane or a fight from off-screen and swing the map. Lean into that. Forcing a straight 1v1 into him after 6 just feeds his scaling — your value is the global engage, not winning the man-to-man.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a coin-flip skirmish — you land Justice Punch into a released taunt if he burned Soul Unbound, and he resets the trade for free if he held it, so count the 22 seconds. Level 6 is your one clear stage: Hero's Entrance means a losing duel doesn't matter, because you R to a sidelane from off-screen and swing the map. Lean into that. Forcing a 1v1 after 6 just feeds a champion whose Spirit Cleave shield returns faster the more attack speed he buys.

notes: Fate Sealed was described as a 'knockup-dash' in two places; it is a blink behind the last champion in a line plus a pull, which changes the positioning rule from 'do not get airborne' to 'do not line up with your team'. Galio facts verified at wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio and reused across this slice: Shield of Durand cuts magic 25/30/35/40/45% and physical exactly half (12.5/15/17.5/20/22.5%), passive magic shield 7.5/9/10.5/12/13.5% max health restoring after 12/10/8s untouched, taunt applied on release. Justice Punch knocks up 0.75s, cannot be interrupted mid-travel, disabled while Grounded, halts on terrain or champions. Winds of War 825, tornado 2s, no slow. Hero's Entrance channels 2.75s, CC-immune after 1.25s. Colossal Smash is a 5s empowered auto scaling with 60% bonus MR. Galio kit-file flag misfires: E tagged 'terrain' and missing 'knockup' despite Riot's description.
